Annette Lawless - What's your take on "thoughts and...
Vice President JD Vance shared his thoughts, as he responded to comments made by former White House Press Secretary Jen Psaki.
This is what she posted online after the deadly shooting at Annunciation Catholic Church this week that killed two children and injured over a dozen other people.
I haven’t read every comment here so don’t know if this has been said, but my take is what an African proverb says: “When you pray, move your feet.” In other words, we should DO something, too.
I agree that prayer can be powerful; but if my child had literally been *praying* in that church yesterday and I was making funeral arrangements today, thoughts & prayers would be cold comfort.
I’d be interested to hear what further action Vance is inspired to take.
“What good is it, my brothers, if a man says he has faith, but has no works?
Can faith save him?
“And if a brother or sister is naked and in lack of daily food, and one of you tells them, ‘Go in peace.
Be warmed and filled;’ yet you didn’t give them the things the body needs, what good is it?
“Go in peace, be warmed and filled” is the kind of easy thing that rolls off the tongue that a person might say who has no real intention to do anything substantive to help.
“Thoughts and prayers” could easily be the same kind of cliche.

Replace “if a brother or sister is naked and in lack of daily food” with “if a brother or sister has lost a child in another school shooting,” and replace “go in peace, be warmed and filled” with “thoughts and prayers,” and a description of a dead, phony faith writes itself.
According to the Washington Post, in the past 26 years in the US, starting with Columbine High School, there have been 390 K-12 shootings, yielding 203 deaths and 441 injuries.

The inaction to ban military-grade assault rifles in the US in that time is testament to a dead, hypocritical faith, and what has turned “thoughts and prayers,” for the most part, into a cruel cliche.
The children who were killed in Minneapolis were literally thinking about God, and praying to Him, when they were shot.
That didn’t save them from the inaction of “thoughts and prayers” politicians.
